claims.statement: Detour authoring state lives in its own zustand store (`createDetourStore` / the `useDetourStore` singleton), separate from the base plotting store: it owns the split/merge nodes, detour stops, the road-followed loop, label and instructions, additional distance, its own history and draft, and it never writes the base plotting store.

The detour editor is opened with a snapshot target built by `buildDetourTarget` from a loaded direction (directionId, directionLabel, routeId, routeName, basePolyline, existingDetourCount, chain-ordered stops); `openNew` resets to IDLE_STATE with the auto label `Detour {existingDetourCount + 1}`, `openEdit` enters `waypoint` mode pre-filled from the saved entity and keeps it as `editBaseline`, and the direction's stops are late-bound exactly once through `setTargetStops` because the directions list response does not embed stops.

Placement is a three-phase click machine (`mode`: entry → exit → waypoint). In the two node phases each click is projected onto the base polyline with a 5000 m corridor; a click outside the corridor sets `composeError` and places nothing.

The merge (exit) node must lie strictly further along the base arc than the split (entry) node: `snap.index < entry.index || (snap.index === entry.index && snap.fraction <= entry.fraction)` is refused as `{ kind: "order" }`, the refused projection is retained so `swapEntryExit()` can accept it as the split in one action, and `mode` stays `exit` until a valid merge lands.

A split/merge pair closer than 30 m (`NODE_TOO_CLOSE_METERS`) is refused client-side as `{ kind: "degenerate" }` with `exit` left unset, mirroring the server's 30 m degeneracy tolerance so a composition that passes the client gate is not refused for the same reason on save.

In waypoint mode every click appends a detour stop (client-local `crypto.randomUUID()` id, name `Stop {n}`, type `waiting_area`, no guaranteed service, no landmark/notes) and rebuilds the loop; detour stops are deliberately not projected onto the base polyline because they define the diversion; the first stop auto-fills `commuterInstruction` with "Take the detour" only for a new detour whose instruction is still empty, never in edit mode.

The split and merge nodes are draggable markers whose drop is re-projected onto the base polyline through the same 5 km corridor; a drop outside the corridor is ignored, which keeps the persisted `entry`/`exit` on the base line.

The loop is a road-followed line through `[entry, ...detourStops, exit]` produced by an injected `LoopSnapper` (default: `snapPreview` → the admin Mapbox directions proxy, which chunks waypoints at 25), guarded by a module-scope sequence counter that makes builds latest-wins and that is bumped on open, close, undo, redo and draft restore so a pending build cannot land on a composition the admin has left or undone.

Loop-building failure semantics: a thrown snapper falls back to a straight `LineString` through the waypoints and sets `mapboxWarning: "upstream_error"`, while the proxy's degraded `snapped: false` straight-line response resolves as success and is adopted as the loop without any warning, because the store reads only `.polyline` and never inspects `snapped` or `warning`.

The additional distance is derived, never entered: `round(max(0, polylineDistanceMeters(loop) − replacedArcLengthMeters(base, entry, exit)))`, recomputed on every loop rebuild. `replacedArcLengthMeters` honours fractional projections (entry-segment tail + full middle segments + exit-segment head) and returns 0 for out-of-order or identical positions, so a node snapped mid-segment never over-counts a whole segment.

`validateSave()` is a pure client gate that either returns a reason or the exact POST/PUT payload. Its ordered checks are: editor open with a target, split node present, merge node present, at least one detour stop, loop with at least two coordinates, non-blank label, non-blank commuter instruction; on success it trims text, maps `driver_instruction` to null when empty, emits entry/exit as Point GeoJSON and `additional_distance_meters` (or 0). It performs no I/O — the store tests assert the snapper is not called by refuse/pass passes.

The detour panel only issues HTTP after the gate passes: `handleSave` calls the store's save gate (or the edit-patch builder, which validates first) and sends nothing when it refuses, writing the reason to `lastError`; on a server failure the message is written to `lastError` and shown inline and the editor keeps its composition so the admin can retry (SC-014).

A stale-list conflict guard runs before the gate: the direction's detour count captured when the editor opened (`baselineDetourCount`, seeded from `existingDetourCount`) is compared with the current detours query length, and a mismatch refetches the list and refuses the save with the "Another detour was added or removed while you were editing" copy. The guard is count-based, so it detects additions and deletions but not concurrent edits of an existing detour.

Editing a saved detour saves a computed patch of changed fields only: label, commuter instruction, driver instruction, and — when any of the loop, entry or exit changed — the geometry triple `detour_polyline` + `entry` + `exit` + `additional_distance_meters` together, plus `detour_stops` when the projected stop list differs from the baseline. An empty patch is refused with "No changes to save." and the editor stays open.

Detour activation is a detached concern: the `Active` switch in the detour properties panel issues its own `PUT { is_active }` through the update mutation, while the editor's create payload and composed patch never include `is_active` (the shared schema accepts it only on the update schema).

On POST the server requires the direction to exist (404), validates `entry` and `exit` against the direction's base polyline with 30 m tolerance, validates the loop's first/last coordinate against entry/exit within the same tolerance, rejects a degenerate (coincident) entry/exit, and rejects a label already used by another detour of that direction; only then does it insert the detour row and its ordered stop rows and return 201.

On PUT, `entry`/`exit` are re-validated on the base polyline when supplied, and the loop-endpoint (and degeneracy) check runs whenever any of `detour_polyline`, `entry` or `exit` is present — validated against the resulting triple (`body.* ?? current.*`), so replacing only one geometry field cannot drift the loop's endpoints away from its nodes. The label guard excludes the detour being updated.

`detour_stops` is a REPLACE operation on PUT: the payload carries the full ordered list, the handler deletes every row for that detour and re-inserts it, numbering `stop_order` from array position 0..n-1. Omitting the field leaves the stored list untouched, an empty array clears it, and a repeated save therefore mints fresh stop ids — client-local stop ids never survive a save.

A PUT that touches only `detour_stops` must not run an empty SET clause: `detour_stops` is not a `detours` column and never enters the patch object, and the `UPDATE` executes only when `Object.keys(patch).length > 0`, because drizzle renders `update().set({})` as invalid SQL. The integration suite sends exactly such a detour_stops-only PUT and expects 200 with the replaced list.

Detour stops live in their own `detour_stops` table (keyed by `detour_id` with ON DELETE CASCADE and a unique `(detour_id, stop_order)` index) with full base-stop parity fields, and are never part of the base stop chain — the direction's ordered stop list consumed by routing and the dataset export is the separate `stops` table keyed by `direction_id`, which detour authoring never writes. A detour's route is entry (base) → detour_stops in stop_order → exit (base).
Unlike the direction save, the detour POST handler uses no explicit database transaction: the detour row insert and the detour-stop inserts are sequential statements inside one request.

The detour store keeps its own undo/redo capped at 50 entries, recording a full-composition snapshot (mode, nodes, stops, loop, label, instructions, additional distance) before every change, clearing the future branch, and short-circuiting identity writes; undo and redo bump the snap sequence so an in-flight loop build cannot overwrite the restored composition.

Detour drafts are a separate mini-draft from the base plotting draft: full `DetourDraftSnapshot` payloads (composition plus target, editDetourId and baselineDetourCount) written to localStorage under `komyuter.detour-draft.{directionId}` with a 24 h TTL, written per change but only after the composition is `touched`, so a pristine open never clobbers a leftover draft. Restoration resumes editing the same saved detour with the same conflict baseline, and the offer appears once per direction.

The detour draft is cleared only by a successful save (`clearDraft: true` after `close()` so the persistence effect cannot rewrite it), while Cancel, Esc and switching away from the Add tool preserve it for the next restore offer; Discard clears the key and dismisses the offer, and Restore hydrates the store and clears the key.

Keyboard and pointer ownership while the detour editor is open: `mod+s` for the base-route save is disabled and its Save button hidden, `mod+z` / `mod+shift+z` dispatch to the detour store when it is open and to the plotting store otherwise, `Esc` leaves the detour editor first (draft preserved) after the child-dialog and focused-field checks, and every map tap goes to the detour store while the Add tool is active — with any other tool the tap closes the editor — so base stop placement is unreachable until the detour editor closes.

While the editor is open its detour stops are first-class map markers: draggable, rendered hollow/dashed in the base stop-type shape vocabulary, click-selectable, keyboard-editable through `DetourStopGroup` (name, type, guaranteed service, landmark hint, notes — location by dragging only, plus Remove), and the placement of a new stop clears the selection.

`DetourLayer` renders the open direction's saved detours as dashed lines in a stable per-detour colour (inactive detours at reduced opacity) whenever a direction is open — independent of the editor being open — gated by the detour layer toggle and the sidebar's per-detour eye toggle, and draws the live composition as a separate amber dashed loop.

The flanking helper `inferDetourFlanks` — the original one-click detour inference — is no longer used by detour authoring (nodes are explicit) but is reused by the base plotting store as its mid-route insertion rule; the store tests still cover its loop-wrapping behaviour.
